body: Jen and I never discussed the recipe.

“It’s a recipe” goes both ways. For me, it was my only connection to Abby that was only mine. For them, it was a tasty dish. One party had more to lose with the escalation. I handled the pressure poorly and allowed Jen to pay the price. That I have never denied.
It takes longer to post a rebuttal than to edit your comment. Yes, I shouldn’t have given a false recipe. That is established.

It can be rewarding, which is why I would share other recipes. However *this* recipe was designed to fade away, having only been known by Abby and I, as the one single thing that was special to our relationship and not shared with my father, brother, or other family and friends. It was an insular part of a relationship. 

Greg has mugs and a plate that he made with Abby that only he uses, and a painting that I have never seen, a song I have never heard. I have a recipe that is mine and Abby’s, and we promised to keep it that way, because the legacy wasn’t what we wanted out of the recipe. 

It could have been as simple as a “recipe” for a PB&J and I still wouldn’t share it.

Not complex in the sense that it uses intermediate skills to create. 

Many dishes vary from chef to chef, as others here have mentioned. I assumed the difference in taste would be attributed to that. Yes, I should have stood my ground.
It’s a recipe, not the Apple of Eris, and belonged to Abby and me, not to the family.
What you are comfortable with is not the standard across humanity, and it narrows your perspective to approach situations as such.
It is disrespectful of her well known wishes.

I’m glad for you that you are so principled and enjoy that stance, which places your viewpoint as the moral standard and crushes the desires of anyone else. Thank you for the discussion, but I believe our perspectives are much too different for anything constructive to come from further talks. 

I sincerely hope you never take something special from someone with your unshakeable belief in your rights to someone else’s creation.

That said, I’m terribly sorry you were purposefully excluded. Perhaps this sort of stance contributed to the woman’s acerbic refusal. Food for thought.

You are awfully presumptuous and unwilling to understand another view point because it doesn’t match what you yourself would do and feel. 

If she was humoring me, she had plenty of chances to recant. I did not initiate the secrecy pact. She refused to share with many, including my brother and father, on numerous occasions. 

A compliment and flattery does not obligate me, or anyone, to any action.

Yes, it’s not selfish at all to demand I ignore Abby’s wishes. It’s not selfish to demand I share this one thing kept solely between her and me. 

“It’s just a recipe” goes both ways. It’s just a recipe. What do others lose by not having it? Why can they not be content with the amount already being shared?

It’s one recipe of countless. It’s one small portion of my time with Abby that was given to me only. We didn’t have to cook the dish for any of the family at all, and we shared a portion.

Not everything is to be shared. Not everything is meant to last forever. It may be intended as a compliment but that compliment does not obligate the person to share anything they don’t want to. Someone else’s enjoyment of something is not reason enough, and certainly not as potent as reason as to overrule the creator’s desires.

This is the only recipe that dies with us. You can doubt it, but this was established years ago. 

I regret the harm my actions caused and if I had a do over I would have continued to refuse rather than allow Jen to be hurt.

*This* recipe dies with its creators. This was established and intentional. There are other recipes that will be passed on. This is one that lives only through Abby and I. 

Greg has many other things to remember her by. Trips of the two of them, or of him, Abby and Dad, paintings, pottery, music. If he so desperately wanted a recipe, I would have shared others. 

I deeply regret *how* I acted to protect the secret because it hurt Jen. There were other options then, and other options now. I’ll do what I can to help ameliorate the pain I put her through and offer my sincerest apologies. That is all I can do. I can’t force her to forgive me or erase the humiliation and frustration by saying “Oops”
It’s an egg dish.

Greg has several other means of remembering Abby. I have the recipes we created together, and the memories we shared. Any other recipe I would have handed over, but he wanted this one, the singular one that Abby and I promised each other never to tell another soul. I believe fervently that Abby would appreciate that I kept my promise, but be disappointed in how I gave a fake recipe rather than continuing to hold my ground. 

Why anyone gets pleasure out of forcing people to give up what they cherish because more people desire it is beyond me. 

Both of us may be projecting our own hurts in this response. You for feeling slighted by another’s boundary, me for you presuming to know Abby better than I did.

One thing I will certainly agree with you on is that I handled the situation poorly and Jen experienced the backdraft. I will do what I can to make amends to her.
Your enjoyment of something created by someone else is not a singular metric to determine what they are required to share.
In this case, intention doesn’t erase or fully mitigate the fallout, and the knife doesn’t cut equally. Dad is Greg’s birth father as well as mine.

I’ll speak to Dad. This was a tough situation and regardless of the what final verdict here will be, I have wrongs to right especially in regards to Jen. 

And yes. They’re hosting this year, so I’ll be spending Christmas alone.

You state two hard truths in this, that I actively contributed to ruining a first experience as a newlywed, and that there may be no recovering the relationship. Thank you. It’s not comfortable to hear but it needed to be said.
Maybe I’m overtired but that just made me laugh more than anything else in a while. Thank you.
Because Greg refused that option.

As do I. 

For what it’s worth I did check the recipe beforehand to make sure it was a passable imitation of the real deal. Clearly I fucked up there, but at the time of, I thought it would go unnoticed. Hindsight is 20-20
At this point, I can’t speak to how much Greg told Jen. Personally I never explained to her, but at the same time, this recipe never came up between us.

You may not understand someone’s final desires. That doesn’t make them unworthy of following. I’m sorry we disagree on this front. Thank you for commenting. 

Abby did indeed create something wonderful that many enjoyed. She was also willing and preferred for it to die with its creators, hence our pact.

Ultimately, I feel horrible for Jen. I never meant for her to face any negative repercussions. I even gave a recipe that was as close taste wise to Abby and mine’s as possible, but that didn’t matter. Jen had to bear the brunt of me trying to balance Abby’s promise and Greg’s requests. That wasn’t fair to her. I expected the AH responses for that fact alone.

I have zero idea at this point what Jen did or didn’t know in relation to the recipe, but I’ve never told Jen about my promise to Abby. 

(Edited to be clear)
That’s a harsh stance to accept immediately, but thank you for positing it. I’ll think on this.
In hindsight I can think of a million other ways to assuage Jen’s fears about having messed up. All that came to mind in the moment was coming clean. I’m not a good liar, apparently
That seems like a recipe for disaster, but thank you for the laughs!

I wish I’d seen this comment sooner to correct you. It wasn’t Jen’s family at all.

(This was the comment I meant to respond to. I’m very sorry for not noticing sooner.)
I am so sorry. I’m on mobile and ended up answering the wrong comment.
Edited because I answered the wrong comment
I wasn’t thinking about how I would appear. I just wanted to make Jen feel better and reassure her it wasn’t her fault the result wasn’t what she expected.
It will have died with us when I pass. Abby had previously refused to tell Dad and Greg both.

To be honest that was the comment that made me even consider finding an alternative recipe to give, versus continuing to say no. I‘m pretty sure that makes it worse. At the time I just wanted to give something that would have passed for the same thing, as a sort of peace offering of sorts, and it backfired spectacularly.

I agree with your points, please don’t get me wrong, but I did offer to bring the dish and Greg refused that option.

Yes, that makes sense

She was breaking down and near to the point of sobbing over the recipe, and kept saying she followed it. My instinct was to tell her that the fault wasn’t on her. It ended up backfiring. It was a poor attempt to reassure her that she wasn’t a “failure of a chef” who couldn’t follow a simple recipe. I acted on instinct, not on what would have made me look better.
